clinical.title: The clinicians your teen may work with.
clinical.intro: Our clinical team focuses on adolescent behavioral health. Admissions can walk you through who will be part of your teen’s assessment and care.

members.name: Grace Beasley
members.title: Primary Therapist
bio: My therapeutic style is highly collaborative with my clients and person centered. I work with folks ages 10+ who may be struggling socially, at school, or with emotion regulation through techniques such as play therapy, sandtray therapy, parent collaboration, and creative expression. With my clients, I take a person centered approach that combines multiple avenues of expression and options for all ages to increase self-determination, engagement, and empowerment to make a safe space. My approach is to combine art or expressive based activities with evidence based modalities such as DBT (Dialectical Behavioral Therapy), CBT (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy), and ACT (Acceptance and Commitment Therapy) with a trauma informed lens. I am always looking to learn more and increase my knowledge base with modalities such as IFS (Internal Family Systems) and increasing my skills around supporting neurodivergence.

Additionally, I enjoy working with young adults and older teens in a time of life transition who may be figuring out their pathways towards independence amid their own mental health challenges or stress of the future. Adolescents have such strengths and challenges today and my goal is to support their journey in self-exploration, while finding ways to support their mental health that make sense for their needs.

I received my Master of Social Work from North Carolina State University and was in a fellowship program that furthered education on trauma, especially in adolescents, LGBTQIA+ affirming practices, and at-risk youth. My master’s internship was working with adolescents in an IOP (Intensive Outpatient Program), working with teens who were living through depression, suicidal ideation, self-harm, anxiety, and trauma. After my education and internship, I found a passion for the IOP level of care and for the uniqueness of adolescents’ stage of life. I continued collaborating with families and their teens who were encountering life struggles, self-harm, depression, school refusal, and ADHD/ASD. With my teens, I also prioritize caring for the whole family unit. I enjoy working with families to help parents find techniques/skills that work for their child(ren’s) unique needs and increase family cohesion. Our support systems are so important and I am always looking to help empower families to find connection in the midst of challenges.

members.name: Beth Bertram
members.title: IOP Clinical Lead
bio: I’m passionate about creating a safe, welcoming space where all clients feel heard, valued, and empowered. My approach is grounded in compassion, curiosity, authenticity, and respect for each client’s unique experience. I affirm and celebrate all identities.

I earned my bachelor’s degree from Anderson University (Indiana) and began my professional career at a Child Advocacy Center, where I worked as a forensic interviewer and victim advocate. In this role, I worked closely with children and families navigating investigations of abuse and neglect.

I later earned my master’s degree from Indiana University. Following graduation, I worked as an intensive in-home therapist supporting families involved with the juvenile justice system or child protective services. Most recently, I have worked as an outpatient therapist serving children, teens, and young adults. In this role, I was also intensively trained as a Dialectical Behavior therapist, working with individual DBT clients and leading multifamily DBT groups.

I have training and experience in several evidence-based practices including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Family Centered Treatment (FCT), Motivational Interviewing (MI), mindfulness practice, and Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (TF-CBT). I tailor these approaches to support clients with a variety of diagnoses and concerns including anger, anxiety, communication, depression, domestic violence, emotion regulation, life transitions, and PTSD.

members.name: Hannah Pridemore
members.title: Clinical & Community Outreach
bio: My heart for helping families comes from seeing firsthand the impact mental health can have on the people we love. Having family members who have experienced mental health challenges has given me a deep appreciation for how important it is to have supportive people in your corner. That's why I am dedicated to helping families find hope, guidance, and the right support when they need it most.

I earned my bachelor's degree in Psychology from Duke University and later completed my master's degree at Duke University's Fuqua School of Business. While I'm not a clinician, I have the privilege of being one of the first people families and referral partners connect with. My goal is to make the process feel approachable, supportive, and hopeful from the very first conversation.

I joined Joshua Tree Health because I immediately connected with Gabriela's vision and dedication to creating a place where teens and families receive exceptional, evidence-based care. I love building relationships throughout the community and helping families find relief during what is often one of the hardest seasons of their lives. If I can help a parent take a deep breath and feel confident they're in the right place, I've done my job.

Outside of work, you'll usually find me spending time with my five nieces and nephews (all under six!), volunteering, cheering on the Duke Blue Devils, watching just about any sporting event, or hanging out with my two dogs: Casper, my Pyredoodle (Great Pyrenees and Standard Poodle mix), and James, my French Bulldog.

Whether you're a parent looking for guidance or a provider searching for resources, please don't hesitate to reach out. I believe no family should have to navigate a mental health crisis alone, and I'm always happy to be a resource, answer questions, and help connect your family or patient with the support they need.

members.name: Corissa Phannenstill
members.title: Qualified Professional
bio: I’m dedicated to fostering a safe, supportive, and non-judgmental space where all individuals are valued, respected, and understood. My areas of interest include emotional regulation, LGBTQIA+ populations, intersectionality, and social-emotional development. My approach is grounded in a strengths-based perspective, emphasizing each person’s strengths for the capacity for growth.

I earned my bachelor’s degree in Social Work from the University of Wisconsin-Whitewater and will be working towards my master’s degree in the future. I also have a certificate in LGBTQ+ Studies and Women’s and Gender Studies.
During my undergraduate degree internship, I worked alongside a non-profit organization providing advocacy and support to survivors of domestic violence.
I enjoy reading, photography, spending time with family and friends, and finding new restaurants and coffee shops.

members.name: Mariah Echevarria
members.title: Psychiatric Physician Assistant
bio: Mariah is a Florida native who earned her Bachelor of Science from the University of Florida and her Master of Physician Assistant Studies from the University of South Florida. She has over four years of experience providing outpatient psychiatric care to patients ages 5 and older, treating a wide range of mental health conditions.

Her clinical interests include anxiety, OCD, ADHD, trauma, women’s mental health, and life transitions. Mariah is passionate about creating a supportive, patient-centered environment where individuals feel heard, respected, and empowered through shared decision-making. She is also a strong advocate for compassionate, individualized care that recognizes the whole person.

In addition to clinical practice, Mariah serves as an adjunct instructor at the University of South Florida, where she teaches behavioral health to future physician assistants. Outside of work, she enjoys spending time with her dogs, Sunnie and Skye, getting lost in a good book, and trying new hobbies and adventures.

members.name: David Wingfield
members.title: Therapy Intern & Educational Liaison
bio: I am a Master of Social Work student at Liberty University with a concentration in Individual and Family Clinical Practice. My background in education, behavioral health, and outpatient counseling has given me the opportunity to work alongside adolescents and families navigating anxiety, depression, life transitions, and relationship challenges. I am passionate about creating a space where clients feel comfortable showing up as themselves without fear of judgment.

My approach is grounded in empathy, authenticity, and genuine connection. I enjoy helping clients better understand themselves, build confidence, and develop practical tools to navigate life's challenges. I believe growth and healing begin when people feel seen, heard, and supported.

members.name: Ashley Masingale
members.title: Therapy Intern
bio: I hold a Bachelor of Social Work degree from North Carolina State University and am currently enrolled in the Advanced Standing Master of Social Work program at the University of North Carolina, working toward clinical licensure.

My passion for the arts, nature, and outdoor activities informs my approach to creating meaningful and impactful connections in practice with clients. I emphasize autonomy, empowerment, and creativity in my approach; I’m especially drawn to DBT, expressive arts, and trauma-informed practices as ways to help clients build skills, process experience, and discover themselves. I value curiosity and acceptance and am committed to cultivating spaces where these values can flourish.

I enjoy rock climbing, figure skating, doing theatre, and I’m a proud gecko mom! Whether I’m on a climbing wall, on the ice, or on stage, I find that staying creative and active outside of work keeps me grounded and better able to show up for the people I work with.
